requirement:
`habeas mdbook` automatically generates one documented-coverage-gaps
subchapter under the requirements index of {cite}`requirements.index.chapter`,
whether that index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.
rationale:
The requirement has two testable obligations. `habeas mdbook` must generate exactly one documented-coverage-gaps subchapter under the requirements index. It must do so both when the index is explicitly placed and when it is automatically generated. The tests cover both cases.

- **Explicitly placed index:** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` puts a `{requirements-index}` directive in a chapter. It then filters the index's sub-items for chapters named "Documented coverage gaps" and asserts `coverage.len() == 1`. It also asserts the chapter's path (`appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md`) and its `parent_names` (`["Requirements index"]`). Finally, it asserts the index content links to `requirements-index/coverage.html`.
- **Automatically generated index:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` has no marker directive. It asserts that the generated top-level "Requirements index" has exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" sub-chapter. It also asserts the path `requirements-index/coverage.md`, the parent name, and the index link. It checks that the detail pages are separate and do not include the coverage chapter.
- **Generated chapter's content and placement:** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` runs `populate_in` for a requirements index placed under a parent chapter, once with a section number and once without. It checks the link in the parent's content, the chapter's path, parent names and numbering, and the guidance text. It also checks that the `:::{coverage-index}` directive is replaced.

A generator that skipped the chapter, duplicated it, or attached it to the wrong parent would fail these assertions. The tests make no assertion about a failure case that the requirement text does not name, and none is required. No gaps are found.

text: subchapter under the requirements index of {cite}`requirements.index.chapter`,
whether that index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.

An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
